label: Faithful origin-tolerance countermodel to the actual-world Euclidean inert arrival
paraphrase: Closed mathematical controls, every individual counted concrete, natural-number times. (1) Five worlds, two individuals a and b, origins on three offsets near iff they differ by at most one step: a has offsets -1, 0, +1 at aMinus, actual, plus; b has offsets 0, 0, -1, +1 at actual, plus, bMinus, bPlus; a is absent from bMinus and bPlus, b from aMinus; access fails only between aMinus and plus and between bMinus and bPlus. Closeness is a tolerance, access is determined by origin closeness, every near origin variation is realised, and a has non-near origins at two successors of actual. Actual accesses itself, presence-to-existence, inert emptiness and the possible contingent-free past at actual (witness plus, times 0 < 1) hold; Euclidean access at actual fails and no individual exists at actual and every world accessible from actual. (2) On the three-offset tolerance frame with one individual existing at every offset with that offset as origin, the same four origin commitments hold and that individual exists at actual and every accessible world. Statements about these finite interpretations only. Scope (semantic challenge 2026-11-10): faithful only to the encoded origin-tolerance commitments (rigid identity; Salmon-style access iff shared individuals have near origins, whose if-half is OPEN; near-origin plenitude; one varied individual), with stipulated absences (a from bMinus and bPlus, b from aMinus) and a stipulated temporal profile not tied to origins; model-witnessed for this finite encoding only. Not tested: counterpart, vague or kind-relative tolerance, or recombination/deletion plenitude.
